_meta.indication: Treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause

pivotal_trials.phase: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical trial (phase not stated in label)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter; women randomized 1:1 to LYNKUET 120 mg or placebo once daily at bedtime for 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Menopausal women with moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms; mean age 54.6 years (range 40-65)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change in frequency and severity of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms from baseline to Weeks 4 and 12
pivotal_trials.n: 796 women randomized (OASIS 1: LYNKUET N=199, placebo N=197)
pivotal_trials.result: OASIS 1: VMS frequency change from baseline to Week 12 difference vs. placebo -3.22 (95% CI -4.81, -1.63), P<0.0001; VMS severity Week 12 difference -0.40 (95% CI -0.54, -0.25), P<0.0001

pivotal_trials.phase: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical trial (phase not stated in label)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter; women randomized 1:1 to LYNKUET 120 mg or placebo once daily at bedtime for 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Menopausal women with moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change in frequency and severity of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms from baseline to Weeks 4 and 12
pivotal_trials.result: OASIS 2: VMS frequency change from baseline to Week 12 difference vs. placebo -3.24 (95% CI -4.60, -1.88), P<0.0001; VMS severity Week 12 difference -0.29 (95% CI -0.44, -0.14), P<0.0001

key_safety: Most frequently reported (>5%) adverse reactions were headache, fatigue, dizziness and somnolence. In OASIS 3: headache 9.6% vs 7.0% placebo, fatigue 7.3% vs 2.9%, dizziness 6.1% vs 1.9%, somnolence 5.1% vs 1.3%. Nervous system effects occurred in 11.9% on LYNKUET vs 3.5% placebo. Transaminase elevations ≥3x ULN occurred in 0.6% vs 0.4% placebo.
target_moa: Neurokinin 1 (NK1) and neurokinin 3 (NK3) receptor antagonist; inhibition of Substance P and Neurokinin B through antagonism of NK1 and NK3 receptor signaling on KNDy neurons modulates thermoregulation associated with hot flashes
modality: Small molecule (elinzanetant capsules, for oral use)

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary

summary.text: Standard NDA under section 505(b) received July 26, 2024 and approved in 2025 for moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause; not referred to an advisory committee; pediatric study requirement waived.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) received July 26, 2024, and your amendments, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Lynkuet (elinzanetant) capsules.
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.
We are waiving the pediatric study requirement for this application because necessary studies are impossible or highly impracticable.
